column1: # One row per benchmark, in report order. Every listed benchmark MUST have
# an implementation in each of its languages (<name>.nu, .c, .rs, and .js
# and .py for the five-language rows) and all of them must print the same
# single line; `bench/bench.sh` refuses to time a row whose outputs
# Columns: name <TAB> blurb <TAB> what it measures [<TAB> languages]
# The optional fourth column lists the row's languages, space-separated;
# left out, it is all five (nurl c rust node python). NURL, C and Rust are
# required on every row — they are the columns wasmbench.sh rotates and the
# only ones with a BENCH_SCALE multiplier. The crypto rows are NURL/C/Rust
# only: their NURL side calls the standard library's own implementation
# (stdlib/std/*.nu), and a pure-JS/pure-Python port of a 64-bit cipher
# would measure BigInt, not the language; Node and Python print `n/a`.
# Benchmarks that live in this directory but are NOT listed here are not
# part of the timing suite: brackets, csv_sum, histogram, quicksort, rot13
# and words are the held-out corpus for the generation-accuracy study in
# genacc/ (their workloads are single short strings — they measure process
# start-up, not a language), and http_server belongs to run_http.sh.
